children.name: Desktop shell
children.summary: The main process, preload and renderer. Finds the cbi binary on PATH, maps the open project, watches the worktree, and switches worktrees and branches. It shows the last built map at once, toasts when a background scan changes it, opens one file in the editor from a matching worktree or a read-only git show snapshot, shows a deep-link window without focusing it, and shows a banner when a newer release is known.

children.name: Deep links
children.summary: cbi://open links. The CLI builds a link and macOS open launches the app; the app checks the repo, ref, node and comparison, then switches the existing window.

children.name: App packaging
children.summary: Copies the Electron window's index.html and style.css into app/dist. The app package.json build script runs this before the desktop app is packaged.

concepts.name: Desktop app
concepts.summary: The Electron shell. It runs the installed cbi CLI, keeps recents and view state outside the repo, and shows the start screen beside the concept map.

concepts.name: Static viewer
concepts.summary: The concept map opened from file://. The build copies the page and writes data/concepts.js, and the page lays boxes out with elk, falling back to deployables when the model has no concepts. The page can copy a node's agent block and open one file in the editor; a static ref view copies a git show command instead.

children.name: Command line
children.summary: The cbi entry point. Argparse dispatches every command, from init and scan through tasks, queries, diff, render, open and review. cbi check fails when changed files have no summary or owner, or when a git ignore rule hides the team judgement, cbi open-file launches the editor from a matching worktree or a read-only git show snapshot, and prime and status print a one-line notice when a newer release is known.

children.name: Scanning and enumeration
children.summary: Lists tracked files with git, hashes the working tree, assigns stable node ids, and links markdown mentions. A ref scan reads blobs with git cat-file and does not check the commit out.

children.name: Parsing and resolution
children.summary: Tree-sitter parsers for Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Vue and C#, then import, call, test, env and reference resolution from the stored facts. HTTP client calls are linked to the server routes they match.

children.name: Manifests
children.summary: Detects deployables and packages from package.json, pyproject, Vite, Docker, compose, wrangler and skills, applies .cbi/structure.json, and follows imports from each entry point.

children.name: Judgement tasks
children.summary: The task protocol and the prime guide, which can read a stored ref model with --ref. Briefs, validation, bottom-up blocking, and summaries cached in the shared answer database. A large brief splits into parts. Team mode commits that judgement into the repo and removes a plain root .cbi ignore rule so git can see it.

children.name: Concepts and screens
children.summary: Projects .cbi/concepts.json and .cbi/screens.json on every scan: concept and external nodes, owns and relates edges, screen sketches, and entry points.

children.name: Queries
children.summary: search, show, tests-for, status and cbi context, the reviewer queries (hotspots, orphans, cycles, deps), and ingest of lcov, coverage.py JSON and JUnit XML. cbi context writes a short Markdown block for pasting into an agent.

children.name: Diff
children.summary: Compares two models by stable id. Reports concept structure, relationships, integrations, deployables, env vars, symbols, tests and moves.

children.name: Review
children.summary: Resolves a pull request, branch or commit range, diffs the two commits, and writes review.md. --post edits the inspector's earlier GitHub comment.

children.name: Architecture history
children.summary: Builds an architectural timeline from immutable default-branch models, using direct commits before the first merge and merge commits after it, projects the current concepts onto historical files, compares successive points, and renders cached narratives as a changelog.

children.name: Diff and review
children.summary: Compares two models and writes the change review: a cbi:// link, a Mermaid diagram, and an optional GitHub comment.

children.name: Rendering
children.summary: Renders one concept-map view to PNG and SVG by opening a staged viewer page in headless Chrome. The capture waits until the page sets cbi-render-ready, then reads the screenshot and the SVG and kills that browser.

concepts.name: Mapper
concepts.summary: The Python package behind the cbi command: enumeration, parsing, manifests, judgement tasks, concepts, queries, diff, review and rendering.

concepts.name: Model store
concepts.summary: The SQLite model at .cbi/model.db: nodes, edges, parse facts, tasks, diagnostics, coverage and the full-text index.

concepts.name: Release notes
concepts.summary: Prints one Keep a Changelog section for a version. Given a version and a path to CHANGELOG.md, it writes that section to stdout.

concepts.name: Release check
concepts.summary: Checks the GitHub releases API for a newer stable version and does not install it. The desktop side compares semver, ignores drafts and prereleases, picks the asset for this OS and arch, and stores the etag, the skipped version and the once-a-day banner. The CLI side caches one line for a day under the platform cache or CBI_CACHE_DIR, and a timeout, a draft or a bad response stays inside the check.

externals.name: git
externals.summary: The git command. Enumeration, ref scans, repo checks, merge-base and read-only snapshots all use a fixed argv, never a shell.

externals.name: gh
externals.summary: The GitHub CLI. Used read-only to resolve a pull request, and by cbi review --post to publish the comment.

externals.name: Chrome
externals.summary: Headless system Chrome or Chromium. cbi render and cbi review use it to screenshot the map and read the SVG back.

externals.name: Answer cache
externals.summary: The shared SQLite cache at ~/.cache/codebase-inspector/answers.db, moved with CBI_CACHE_DIR. File summaries are reused across repositories.

externals.name: macOS open
externals.summary: The macOS open command. cbi open hands it a cbi:// URL so Launch Services starts the desktop app or focuses the running one.

externals.name: Editor
externals.summary: VS Code or Cursor. cbi open-file and the desktop app launch a fixed argv, with no shell. A static page uses that editor's URL scheme instead.

externals.name: sqlite3
externals.summary: The sqlite3 command. The desktop app reads status and file rows from model.db with a fixed argv, so the window can open before a scan.

externals.name: GitHub releases
externals.summary: The GitHub releases API for this repository. The update checks GET /releases/latest with an etag and a codebase-inspector user agent. The desktop app then opens the release page or the matching asset in the browser.

answer.summary: The cbi command-line tool, installed from pyproject.toml with its entry at src/cbi/cli.py. It scans a git repository into a SQLite model, runs judgement tasks, and serves search, show, diff, review, render and the static viewer build. prime and status also print a one-line notice when a newer GitHub release is known, and that check does not install anything.

The cbi command-line application scans Git repositories into a SQLite architecture model, supports structured queries and judgement tasks, and builds or renders interactive views, diffs, reviews, and history. It ships the Python mapping engine and its command entry point.

The app package.json build script. It runs copy-assets.mjs, which creates app/dist and copies the window's index.html and style.css into it. It does not compile TypeScript or package the Electron app.

The Codebase Inspector desktop app. Electron starts at app/src/main.ts, which shows the concept-map viewer, runs the cbi CLI to scan and build a project, handles cbi://open links, and opens a file in the user's editor.

The cbi command-line tool, started at src/cbi/cli.py. It scans a git repository into a SQLite model, serves search and review queries, builds the static concept-map viewer, and diffs, renders and reviews changes between commits.

The `cbi` command-line application scans Git repositories into a SQLite architecture model and ships commands for querying, reviewing, comparing, validating, rendering, and maintaining that model. It also manages human judgement tasks, concept and screen maps, test evidence ingestion, editor links, and architecture history.

The cbi command-line tool, started at src/cbi/cli.py. It scans a git repository into a SQLite model, serves search and review queries, builds the static concept-map viewer, and diffs, renders and reviews changes between commits. prime and status also print a one-line notice when a newer release is known.

The cbi command line tool, a Python package whose entry point is src/cbi/cli.py. It maps a git repository, its working tree or any stored ref, into a SQLite model of deployables, packages, files, symbols, tests, env vars, endpoints and schemas, hands judgement back to an agent as tasks, and answers queries over the result. It also ships the static viewer build, structural diff, architecture history and review, `cbi check` for CI, team mode, coverage ingest and editor and deep link launching.

The Codebase Inspector desktop app. Electron starts at app/src/main.ts, which shows the concept-map viewer, runs the cbi CLI to scan and build a project, handles cbi://open links, opens a file in the user's editor, and checks GitHub for a newer release without installing it.

Ships the Electron desktop application for browsing CBI maps across repositories, worktrees, branches, commits, and pull request comparisons. It provides project and version switching, background scan and rebuild coordination, deep links, safe editor opening, recent and view state, update notices, and a tightly constrained bridge to the CBI and Git command-line tools.

Ships the cbi command-line application for building and querying an evidence-backed model of a codebase. It scans worktrees and immutable refs across supported languages, resolves architecture and tests into SQLite, runs judgement workflows, generates static viewers and reviews, compares history, ingests coverage, checks team answers, and safely opens mapped source locations.

answer: Builds a synthetic model to test the viewer payload produced from concepts, symbols, tests, environment variables, screens, externals, re-exports, and declared relationships. It verifies evidence rollups and stated backing, entry and hosting metadata, deployable fallback maps, and generated viewer data files.

Node tests for the background-scan toasts. An unchanged fingerprint, or one that is not yet shown, produces no toast, while a different build names how many files changed, or just says the map updated when the count is zero. A scan error keeps the full output as detail and shortens the first line, ending a long line with an ellipsis.

Tests screen discovery, sketch-task briefs, accepted answers, and viewer projection for Vue components, Django and Razor templates, and Electron HTML pages. It also verifies route, include, and renderer metadata, excludes test and internal render decoys, and rejects detected templates that are neither sketched nor explicitly explained.

Node tests for opening a viewer file in an external editor without a shell. They cover template splitting so a spaced path stays one argument, worktree opens, missing files, ref opens that reuse a worktree with that branch or commit, and read-only git show snapshots that are reused. They refuse paths that leave the project, including through a symlink, look up code on PATH then the macOS app bundle (code.cmd and LocalAppData on Windows), reject editor none and a custom template without {file}, record argv under CBI_EDITOR_DRY_RUN, and reset damaged settings to vscode.

The command line entry point for cbi. It builds the argparse parser for every subcommand, runs the scan pipeline on the working tree or on a stored ref model, and dispatches to handlers for querying, tasks and submissions, rendering, review, history, diff, build, ingest, check, team and opening files. It also passes --out or --ref through to `cbi prime`, prints update notices, and handles broken pipes and Windows UTF-8 output.

Playwright Electron smoke for opening a symbol on a git ref that has no checkout. On macOS it exits unless CI is set, then sets CBI_HEADLESS=1 and CBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 and fails if any window is visible or focused. It builds a side commit that adds src/pay.py, scans and builds that ref, switches the viewer to the read-only side branch, double-clicks arrears, and checks the read-only toast, one dry-run code --goto argv aimed at a mode 0444 snapshot under CBI_SNAPSHOT_DIR, that the fake code binary never runs, and that status, HEAD, and the main checkout stay unchanged.

Playwright smoke test that opens the generated concept viewer from a file:// URL. It builds a fixture model with this worktree's cbi into /tmp/cbi-p19-smoke, then checks pan, zoom, fit, drill-in and back, grey-node selection and jump, and search for a symbol and an env var. Failures exit non-zero, and screenshots are written beside the fixture.

Turns cbi worktrees --json into switcher targets: worktrees, local branches, and remote-tracking branches only after a fetch. Keys are worktree:, branch:, remote: and compare:; a checked-out branch opens its worktree, while other branches and remotes are read-only refs, and usableRef refuses a name that could change argv. initialTarget opens a picked linked worktree or else restores the last key then the main worktree, and formatScanned plus refInstruction supply the header and the cbi tasks --ref prompt.

Tests large-brief parts, draft checks, task paging, and concurrent submits. A brief header states its byte size, and tasks accept limit and offset. Define-concepts splits by package plus a cross-area part when over budget, --check reports missing files without submitting or closing the task, screen parts keep each component's JSX whole, the current concept map is printed in only one part, prime mentions --parts only when a brief exceeds the budget, and four summarise-files submits from separate processes all succeed.

Preload for the map view. It exposes window.cbiOpenInEditor, which asks the main process to open the given file and line in the configured editor. The map page stays sandboxed; this is the only bridge it gets.

State-aware guide that cbi prime prints for an agent meeting the tool. Three states: the repo is not initialised or not scanned, judgement tasks are still open, or the map is complete. It explains that cbi maps a git repository into a queryable model, never calls a model and never runs the repo's code, and names the next command for the current state, including which task kinds are open or blocked.

Copies the desktop app's static page files into the build directory. From this script's location it resolves the app folder, creates app/dist if needed, and copies src/index.html and src/style.css into dist.

Finds executables the app spawns, including git, cbi, code, and cursor. findOnPath walks PATH for platform filenames (the bare name off Windows, .exe then .cmd then the bare name on Windows, with .cmd first for code and cursor), then extra paths, then Windows where, and skips where on a non-Windows host. commandExecutable caches a process PATH hit and otherwise returns the bare name so a later spawn can fail with ENOENT, and missingGit returns a platform-specific install message.

Tests summarise-group and summarise-workspace. Group tasks stay blocked until file and subgroup summaries exist, briefs name the members, and a bad group answer is rejected; display overrides survive a rescan, resubmitting the same text is idempotent, and a parent reopens only when the text changes. A second repo with identical files needs no tasks, a package with no summary task is listed once as its folder, a package with its own summary stays beside that folder and gets a group task, prime reports pending then complete work, and prime before a scan says the repo is not mapped yet.

Resolves an input path to its repository's main working tree and branch using a tightly allowlisted set of read-only Git commands. It handles linked worktrees, submodules, separate Git directories, older Git versions, and clear error cases.

Tests cbi context, a short Markdown block for one symbol, concept, or env node. The block names kind, id, owning concept, calls, tests, integration points, and follow-up commands, drops env values and secrets, and stays within a line cap by dropping extra bullets while keeping commands. Custom --out, --ref, and --compare flags appear on those commands, embed matches render, build writes data/context.js, a missing node or a bad compare range fails, and the viewer sources expose Copy for agent.

Locks the structural diff: a signature-only edit keeps the body hash, one scanned pair emits every EXPECTED kind grouped by concept and matching the golden files, and a bad model fails closed. Two refs scan once and are reused, the same pair reports no changes, and the worktree stays clean. A copied body is not a move; without concepts, groups are deployable then folder; a moved test is omitted and a tests edge on a class or file covers a method; production injection calls count and test calls do not; JSX weight and non-component calls are ignored, and a new component edge is render-added.

Turns a stored recent project into the row the Projects list draws, using the cached branch, task state, task count, and missing flag so the list does not ask git or cbi. A missing folder shows no branch and no tasks. A row that has never been cached is unknown, and the caller can mark it as still refreshing.

Tests scanning immutable Git refs and completing their judgement tasks without checkout or repository mutation, including submodules and missing gitlink objects. It verifies answer-cache reuse, strict read-only Git commands, and worktree and branch inventory JSON.

Pytest coverage of the CLI update check. With a fake fetch and one local server it checks that a newer release is cached for a day, same and older releases say nothing, semver orders double digits, prereleases and drafts are ignored, offline and a hung fetch do not raise, a 304 reuses the cache, CI and CBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK skip the check, and the cache file follows CBI_CACHE_DIR or the platform directory. It also checks that --version prints the version and that prime and status print the notice.

Node tests for finding the cbi executable and storing its path. They check that CBI_BIN wins when it is executable and errors when it is not, that a saved path beats PATH and is not replaced when it is wrong, that PATH is searched before ~/.local/bin/cbi, and that Windows looks for cbi.exe on PATH, then in the user local bin, then via where. A missing binary's error mentions `uv tool install .`, and settings round-trip while damaged JSON reads as unset.

Dispatches one source file to the Vue, C#, Python or TypeScript parser during a scan and returns symbol and test nodes with stable IDs and parent IDs, plus resolution facts. The symbol content hash is the body with the signature stripped, so a rename still matches as a move. Call, read, env, use and HTTP facts are rewritten from definition indexes onto those node IDs, and a spread of process.env stays on the file as an env read of *.

Tests repository initialization and incremental scanning across source files, tests, submodules, symlinks, worktrees, custom output directories, and remote-derived workspace names. It compares golden model dumps, confirms clean Git state, exercises no-change shortcuts and rescan triggers, and checks preservation of later model data.

Runs tests/layout_check.js under node and requires exit 0. The script locks label placement so edge labels miss boxes, stacked pairs collapse to one label, side ranks pick left, right, above, or below, and the render-image key sits below the camera with a 16px margin.

Implements `cbi check`, which scans the repo, reports files changed since the merge base with the default branch that lack a summary or concept owner, and then restores the committed judgement files. It also validates structure.json, concepts.json and screens.json, flags stale or missing team answers, answer text that looks like a key or token, and in team mode a git ignore rule that hides the .cbi/ judgement files. Findings print as text or as GitHub Actions annotations in fail or warn mode.

hotspots ranks files, folders, packages, and concepts by fan-in or symbol count and leaves test files out of the default text. orphans lists unreferenced files, test-only symbols, and files unreachable from deployable entries, counting path.join and HTML script src as references and reporting no unreachable set when there are no entries. cycles names file, folder, and package loops, deps builds a matrix, and --forbid exits 1 with the production imports that match; show orders imports before part_of and prints direct versus transitive membership and env passthrough as prose.

Tests architecture review generation for ranges, branches, and GitHub pull requests, including Mermaid diagrams, images, provisional concept ownership, cached narratives, and comment create-or-update behavior. It verifies merge-base selection, read-only Git behavior, package fallback diagrams, and integration evidence filtering.

Builds and opens a cbi:// link for `cbi open`. It does not write the repo or the model. `run()` accepts a worktree, branch, commit, `--compare base..head` or `--pr` (resolved with `gh pr view --json baseRefOid,headRefOid`), resolves a node id or display name with `query.resolve` when a model exists, prints `cbi://open?repo=&ref=` or `compare=`, and hands that URL to the OS without activating the app (`open -g` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux, ShellExecuteW with SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE on Windows).

Tests cbi check on a team repo. Uncommitted code needs a file summary and a doc does not; a new committed file needs a summary and an owning concept until those tasks are answered, while an edited test keeps its owner. Stale answers, secrets (github format hides the token), and invalid concepts or structure JSON fail; warn mode exits 0 with warning annotations; team.toml brief_budget overrides the environment; the README contains the team init snippet; secret detection skips hex and prose but catches tokens, private keys, and high-entropy strings.

A golden dump locks TS, TSX, and JS imports through index re-exports, tsconfig path aliases, and require(), plus calls for new, static members, export star, namespaces, and JSX, with self calls at confidence 0.6. An unchanged importer is re-resolved when a callee file changes. JSX and React.createElement of an identifier are calls tagged via jsx, a local that shadows the import is not, show labels them renders, and tests-for lists treesitter and naming sources; _jsonc strips comments and trailing commas but keeps // inside strings.

Tests the fixed cbi sequences that produce a map: init, scan, build, and status for a new project, skipping init when already initialised, stopping after a failed scan, and rejecting status that is not JSON. A ref stays one argument, the scan commit and viewer path are recorded, a rebuild does not scan, and a comparison scans both shas then builds with --compare. No step includes a git verb, and the tests also check task state and the agent instruction.

Builds an architectural history from immutable default-branch models and current concept definitions. It selects Git history points, projects concepts onto historical files, compares consecutive models, caches optional pull request metadata and narratives, and renders or writes filtered changelogs.

search finds a class, function, test case, or folder from partial or several unquoted words, filters by display kind or internal kind, and says when nothing matches. show groups relationships, lists tests with the last result and diagnostics, never prints the internal kind, and hides edges under the confidence floor except injection calls unless --all or --min-confidence is set. tests-for returns results and coverage merged across artifacts and does not prefix-match a longer id; status reports scan time, counts, open tasks, and diagnostics, and help names --json, exit codes, and an example.

Node tests for opening an already-built viewer and reading model.db without starting cbi. instantOpen uses the main checkout viewer, a saved worktree viewer, or a ref viewer named by a 40-hex commit, and a picked lane does not fall back to the main map. They also check read-only git rev-parse argv, sqlite3 argv with an immutable file URI, status and file_state parsing, changed-file counts, and payload fingerprints that treat reordered plain lists as the same map.

Pytest for the C# parser and a scanned .NET repository. It checks symbols, XML docs, calls, usings, test attributes and parse errors, then resolution of injection, FromServices factories, namespace usings and configuration reads into the model. A *.Testing.csproj is excluded as a production dependency-injection candidate, and a golden file locks the scanned graph.

Tests team mode for exporting judgement files into Git without committing them and importing answers safely on later scans. It covers initialization, custom output isolation, malformed rows, changed answers, clone reuse, and conflict-free merging of answers produced on separate branches.

Builds a viewer by running a fixed cbi argv and never git. mapProject inits when the ignore file is missing, then scans, builds, and reads status; mapVersion does the same for one worktree or one --ref; mapCompare scans both full shas and then builds with --compare; rebuildViewer rebuilds after the model changes and does not scan. It also reports task state from status JSON, the model directory that owns a viewer, and the agent instruction to run cbi prime.

Tests the cbi prime agent guide and a closed stdout pipe. With --out, prime names that model directory, repeats the open and blocked task counts that scan prints, and omits the note when the model is the repo's own .cbi; it also lists commands for detected node:test, vitest, and pytest runners, including coverage. cbi task and cbi orphans exit 0 with no traceback when stdout is already a closed pipe, and still print normally afterwards.

Builds the static interactive viewer payload from the model, including concepts, relationships, code evidence, tests, environment variables, database and endpoint views, screen sketches, history, and comparisons.

Tests cbi open URL construction and platform launch behavior for worktrees, branches, commits, comparisons, pull requests, and mapped nodes. It validates identifier grammar and injection defenses, fixed read-only Git and gh invocations, ambiguity errors, mutual exclusions, and that opening never changes repository state.

Extracts server routes, router mounts, and HTTP client calls from Python, TypeScript, and C# syntax trees. It resolves path expressions, framework conventions, wrappers, verbs, and handler ownership into endpoint facts.

Tests agent context rendering and embedded viewer context for symbols, concepts, environment nodes, refs, comparisons, and custom output locations. It verifies sensitive values are excluded, long blocks preserve commands, and viewer assets expose the copy-for-agent feature.

Builds environment-variable nodes and the reads_env edges that point at them from parse facts and declaration files. A * read is a whole-environment spread, stored as an env_passthrough diagnostic rather than a variable. Declarations come from .env.example, .env.sample, compose service environment entries and the top-level [vars] table of wrangler.toml; private .env files are never opened, and an example value is taken from the lexicographically first example or sample file that names the variable.

Script for the shell page. It draws the start screen (recent projects, the cbi path, the editor choice, and the automatic update checkbox), the project chrome (branch, task counts, scan progress, and the map-update toast), the update banner, and the worktree, branch, and remote switcher plus the compare form. Actions go through window.cbi, and it reports the map stage's bounds so the main process can place the viewer.

Tests runProcess: the child is spawned with the given argv and shell: false, stdout and stderr are streamed as lines while the exit code is kept, and an argument that contains a space stays a single argument. A process that never exits is killed when the timeout fires, with a non-zero code and stderr matching Timed out.

Tests resolveProject with real git repositories. A nested folder or file resolves to that repo, a linked worktree to the main worktree, detached HEAD is labelled detached, a submodule including its own linked worktree resolves to the submodule rather than the superproject, and a separate git dir resolves to its working tree. A non-repo, a missing folder, and a bare repo are refused; an old git without --path-format still resolves a relative common dir; calls stay on the GIT_ARGV allowlist and the tree stays clean.

Generates architecture reviews by resolving a ref or pull request, scanning both sides, comparing their models, and rendering a Markdown report with diagrams, narrative tasks, and optional screenshots. It can safely create or update a marked GitHub pull request comment and validates its generated Mermaid flowchart locally.

Defines shared pytest fixtures and subprocess safeguards for isolated, cross-platform integration tests. It creates committed temporary repositories, redirects CBI caches, enforces subprocess timeouts, normalizes line endings, and supports executable stand-ins on Windows and POSIX.

On a TypeScript service and its test, scan opens summarise-files, the brief outlines DeviceRegistry with its signature and doc, and submit stores the summaries with a repeat reported as nothing changed. show and search return the class, the method doc, and the summary text, and build writes a viewer whose app.js loads tree.js and does not use innerHTML. Validation errors name the JSON path, a rescan makes the old input_hash stale while an unchanged file keeps its summary, a second repo reuses the answer cache, and show, search, tasks, and build without a model say to run cbi scan.

Tests that isModelChange is true only for model.db, model.db-journal and model.db-wal. A model change makes ProjectSession rebuild and reload the viewer with the hash noted beforehand (the leading # stripped); unrelated files do nothing, a change during a rebuild causes one more rebuild, and a ref model is watched in its own directory. stop cancels a pending rebuild and closes the watch.

Shared TypeScript shapes for the Electron app. They cover a recent project and the row the list draws, scan progress, toasts, cbi status JSON, the open project and its task counts, switcher rows, the resolved cbi binary, and the viewer stage bounds.

Tests editor command templates, executable discovery, settings persistence, and safe file opening for worktrees and historical refs. It covers snapshot caching, path and symlink escape prevention, Windows behavior, dry runs, and custom editor choices.

A golden dump over two uv packages locks nested classes, property and setter ids split by signature hash, identical signatures, and pytest suites and cases. Imports follow relative, absolute, star, src-layout, namespace, and cross-package paths to the defining file; calls cover aliases and function-local imports, self calls stay at confidence 0.6, and shadowed names are dropped. tests edges come from calls, Path(__file__), and importlib scripts, plus a naming fallback, and mocker.patch or patch of a module attribute links the file at 0.8 while patch.dict of the environment stays unmatched.

Python parser. Symbols are definitions at module scope, including inside if, try and with, and in class bodies; functions nested inside functions are not symbols. Facts match the TypeScript shape: imports, calls, literal path reads, os.environ and getenv reads, type-checking imports, injected fields, constructs, pytest cases and mock patch targets, plus HTTP facts from the shared endpoints pass, with module specifiers left for resolve.py.

C# parser for symbols and for xUnit, NUnit and MSTest cases. Namespaces are qualname prefixes, not group nodes; facts are usings, aliases, type mentions, calls, constructor-injected fields, constructs and env reads from Environment and IConfiguration, and nothing is resolved across files. A [Fact], [Theory], [Test] or [TestMethod] method is a test case even when the file was not classified as a test, and test files skip HTTP extraction.

Tests cbi:// links without changing git. File, symbol, test, deployable, env, package, and service ids pass; traversal and injection fail; spaces are names not ids; only base..head compares; PR numbers reject 0, 01, and junk. It prints links for the worktree, branch, full sha, path, node, and compare, and resolves a PR with gh pr view; ambiguous, invalid, unknown, and gh failures exit 1; two version flags exit 2; no handler still prints the link; git argv is read-only; macOS uses open -g, Linux xdg-open drops activation tokens, and Windows uses ShellExecuteW SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE or cmd /c start.

Provides the headless rendering completion hook used to export a stable viewer diagram or screen sketch. It waits for layout, embeds styles, trims the SVG to visible content, and draws an export-friendly legend frame before signaling completion.

Turns a compare form into a plan of two commit refs, or an error. A pull request number is the whole comparison and is read only with gh pr view --json baseRefOid,headRefOid. Otherwise both sides are required: a worktree or branch resolves to the commit it has checked out, and a commit must be a safe ref with no range dots.

Locks the contract of scripts/install-app.sh without running the installer. The script must be executable, start with a bash shebang and set -euo pipefail, reject extra arguments, and contain no sudo, eval, or $1; bash -n must succeed. It must install with uv tool install --force --editable, run npm run package, swap /Applications/Codebase Inspector.app via ditto to dest.new then mv through dest.prev, open -g the new app, roll back with rm and mv on failure, quit the app, and read CFBundleShortVersionString.

Pytest fixtures for the cbi test suite. answer_cache points CBI_CACHE_DIR and CBI_SNAPSHOT_DIR at directories under tmp_path so a test never writes the user's answer cache or snapshot cache. make_repo builds a git repository from a map of relative path to content, commits it, and returns its path.

Desktop update check against the GitHub releases API. It compares stable semver tags, ignores drafts and prereleases, picks the asset for this OS and arch, and caches the etag, the skipped version, and the once-a-day banner in update-check.json. The app does not install the update, and callers open the release page or the matching asset in the browser.

Pytest coverage of Cypress specs, Vue and React route records, and the typeof-import parse workaround. It checks that a vitest file using typeof import parses as tests, that object methods are not routes, and that a scanned fixture records Cypress suites and cases, Vue-router and React-router routes with path, redirect, and guard attributes, and jsx calls from routes to the components they render, including lazy imports. It also checks Cypress visits link to pages and custom commands, show prints guards and redirects, and Cypress specs are left out of orphans and file hotspots.

Command-line entry for cbi. build_parser() registers init, team, scan, check, worktrees, prime, status, search, show, context, tests-for, hotspots, orphans, cycles, deps, tasks, task, submit, ingest, build, diff, render, open, open-file and review, and main() dispatches them. scan writes model.db and scan_ref writes a ref model from git objects with no checkout, the other commands call query, graph, tasks, build, diff, render, review and the rest of the package, and prime and status print a one-line notice when a newer release is known.

Exports the static viewer for `cbi build`. `build()` copies index.html, app.js, style.css, open-editor.js and elk, then writes data/tree.js, data/concepts.js, data/context.js (via `context.embed`), data/diff.js and data/editor.js as cbiLoad scripts and returns index.html. `concept_view()` builds the map (files, symbols, calls, imports, reexports, env, HTTP, tests, coverage, screens, relationships), or deployables, packages and externals when there are no concepts; `compare_payload()` fills data/diff.js with the `cbi diff` change list, removed concepts and the source of each changed function.

sameViewerFile is true when currentUrl is a file: URL for the same viewer index.html, with the hash ignored and invalid URLs returning false. sameViewer also requires the URL hash, without a leading #, to equal the requested hash, so a load of the page already on screen is a no-op.

Looks up the latest GitHub release and returns one line when a newer stable version than this cbi is known. The answer is cached for a day under the platform cache or CBI_CACHE_DIR. A timeout, an offline machine, a draft, a prerelease, or a bad response never raises into the command, CBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 or CI=true skips the check, and nothing is downloaded or installed.

Screen sketches: projects .cbi/screens.json into the model on every scan as one screen node per region tree, parented to the UI concept that owns its root component, with a sketches edge for each region that names a component. This module owns the sketch-screens task, its brief and the checks that every UI-owned component appears in a screen or in unsketched with a reason. Those checks run on submit, not when the file is hand-edited.

Enumerates a git repository and its initialised submodules, hashes tracked file content, applies gitignore-style ignore rules and classifies paths as code, test, doc or other. It builds workspace, group and file nodes, reads one commit's tree from git objects without a checkout, and fingerprints ignore, structure, concepts and screens inputs so a rescan can be skipped. It also inventories worktrees and local branches for cbi worktrees.

Node tests that a Projects row can be drawn from the stored snapshot without calling git or cbi. A never-cached row is unknown rather than missing, a cached missing folder drops the branch and the task count, and the snapshot survives a later open and a reread of the recents file.
Tests icon paths. windowIcon is always the packed build PNG. dockIcon returns that PNG when the app is unpackaged and null when it is packaged, leaving the Dock icon to the bundle.

Structural diff between two model databases, used by cbi diff, which scans both git refs or reuses their stored models and compares stable node IDs. A file or symbol whose content hash is unchanged while its path or qualified name moved is a move; a symbol hash is the body after the signature, so a rename still matches. The result groups concept, ownership, relationship, env, symbol and test changes, plus provisional owners for new files, as text, markdown or JSON.

Node tests for cbi://open links. They check node-id grammar against injection and `..`, URL round-trips including Windows repo paths, viewer hash chips, argv pickup for a second instance, and that git argv stays read-only. Worktree and branch links resolve, traversal and unknown refs are refused, a compare range and `gh pr view` resolve both SHAs, and an unknown query parameter is refused.
Tests cbi prime guidance for custom model output directories and manifest-detected test runners. It also verifies the CLI exits quietly when its stdout pipe is closed.

Implements the Electron main process and application lifecycle for opening projects, versions, deep links, comparisons, and editor targets. It coordinates CBI scans and builds, cached viewers, filesystem freshness checks, recent projects, IPC, updates, menus, and window state.

Pytest coverage of cbi init and cbi scan on a fixture with an initialised and an uninitialised submodule, a tracked symlink, data and fixtures dirs, and build output. It checks ignore rules that keep code-like fixtures and test-data, that scan requires init and leaves git clean, that --out writes the model elsewhere, and that the node dump matches a golden file including symlink, drift, and uninitialised-submodule facts. It also checks workspace naming from the remote or the main folder, when a rescan runs versus the no-change shortcut, and that a rescan keeps a later summary column.

Tests the fixed CBI command sequences used to initialize, scan, build, rebuild, compare, report status, and refresh history. It verifies failure short-circuiting, ref handling, output parsing, and that mapping never invokes Git mutation commands.

Preload for the shell window. With context isolation on, it exposes window.cbi for picking and opening a folder, recents, the cbi binary and editor settings, version switching, compare, toasts, progress, the update banner, and the automatic-check setting, and it sends a dropped file's path to the main process. Each subscription returns an unsubscribe function.

Builds the architecture history from immutable models of the default branch. It picks history points from first-parent history, keeping direct commits made before the first merge and only merge commits after it, scans each point as a ref, projects today's concepts onto that point's files, and records changes and merged pull requests. It also selects and renders entries, writes CHANGELOG-ARCHITECTURE.md, and opens summarise-change narration for one entry.

Playwright checks of the built viewer page. Double-click opens a function while a concept still drills in, and the editor is not launched by the page itself. A ref view copies a git show command instead of following an editor URL.

Playwright test that the viewer's Copy for agent button copies the precomputed context block. Clicking the button or pressing C with Meta or Ctrl copies the selected node's block, shows a Copied toast, and does not change the hash. Copy is left to the browser when text is selected or the search field is focused.

Pytest for Python and container deploy manifests. It checks that pyproject scripts, Dockerfiles, compose services and wrangler workers become deployables, that skills and repertoires become packages, and that compose images become external services with depends_on links. It also covers unresolved entry diagnostics, dropping a removed external on rescan, the YAML reader for anchors and block scalars, and poetry or compose commands mapped to source files.
Creates stable symbol nodes for parsed source files, including definitions, spans, documentation, test metadata, and hashes used to track changes.

Orchestrates CBI mapping workflows for worktrees, refs, and commit comparisons through fixed argument lists. It streams progress, parses status and viewer locations, supports build-only refreshes, and performs optional background history generation.

Playwright Electron smoke for opening a symbol on a git ref that has no checkout. On macOS it exits unless CI is set, then sets CBI_HEADLESS=1 and fails if any window is visible or focused. It builds a side commit that adds src/pay.py, scans and builds that ref, switches the viewer to the read-only side branch, double-clicks arrears, and checks the exact read-only toast, a single dry-run code --goto argv aimed at a mode 0444 snapshot under CBI_SNAPSHOT_DIR in a folder named hq@side-<12 hex>, that the fake code binary never runs, and that status, HEAD, and the main checkout stay unchanged.

Builds the static codebase viewer and serializes tree, concept, context, editor, history, and comparison data into its assets. It derives detailed concept evidence from symbols, tests, coverage, environment reads, imports, HTTP calls, screens, and relationships, with a deployable-based fallback when no concept map exists.

Normalises HTTP paths and links detected client calls to server routes using method, segment, and ownership evidence. It resolves mounted routers and records scored endpoint relationships in the model.

Exercises the core judgement loop from file briefs through accepted summaries and task completion. It verifies JSON-path validation errors, stale-answer rejection after rescans, shared cache reuse across identical repositories, and missing-model errors for read commands.

Binds stored parse facts into edges on every scan the no-change shortcut does not stop. It resolves imports and calls across files, links tests by calls, imports, file names, file reads and patches (a same-file test helper's calls are inherited one level), and writes references edges, http_calls edges and injection calls. It replaces the treesitter, naming and html edges and the ambiguous_call, unmatched_test and unresolved_injection diagnostics, then rebuilds env nodes.
Tests C# parsing and resolution across symbols, documentation, calls, imports, dependency injection, factories, configuration reads, test projects, and golden model output.

Tests the sketch-screens judgement. The task stays absent until concepts are accepted and the repo has UI components; the brief lists component JSX, renders, entries, and state values, and one bad answer reports every check together. Accept writes screens.json and show prints regions; a rescan reopens only when a UI component is new; invalid screens JSON clears screen nodes and reopens the task; a deleted screens.json is restored from the cache; a when condition is accepted and shown, a blank or over-long when is rejected, and screens._read can read a file from a commit-tree object.

Pytest fixtures for the cbi test suite. answer_cache points CBI_CACHE_DIR and CBI_SNAPSHOT_DIR at directories under tmp_path and sets CBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 so a test never writes the user's cache or calls GitHub. make_repo builds a git repository from a map of relative path to content, commits it, and returns its path.

Tests screen discovery and sketch task behavior for Vue routes, Django and Jinja templates, Razor pages, and Electron HTML. It verifies brief evidence, routes, included templates, renderers, accepted screen projection into the viewer, and rejection when detected templates are neither sketched nor explained.

Tests team mode: committed answers, a clone, and a clean merge of answers.jsonl. team init exports judgements, writes a union merge rule into gitattributes without dropping existing lines, and does not commit; outside a git repo it fails, and a non-team repo stays ignored and does not import a hand-written answers file. Import skips bad rows, a changed answers file is imported on scan, --out does not edit the repo, a clone has no open tasks and the same concept map, and two branches merge answers.jsonl without a conflict.

Tests platform-specific command lookup in which.ts. It checks Windows filenames (code.cmd before code.exe, and git.exe or cbi.exe before the .cmd form), a semicolon PATH separator on Windows and a colon elsewhere, and that findOnPath returns an executable from PATH and calls where only as a Windows fallback. It also checks that missingGit names Xcode command line tools, Git for Windows, or installing git, and that commandExecutable returns the bare name git when nothing on PATH is executable.

Reads one query from a model SQLite database by spawning the sqlite3 executable. querySqlite returns null immediately when the database path is empty or contains a null byte. Otherwise it runs sqlite3 with the argument list from sqliteArgs, a 5 second timeout, and a 32 MiB buffer, and resolves to stdout or to null if the command fails.

Tests bottom-up file, group, package, and workspace summary task dependencies, briefs, validation, caching, resubmission, and reopening semantics. It also verifies display overrides, duplicate package handling, cross-repository cache reuse, and prime output before, during, and after completion.
Tests HTTP path normalisation, endpoint extraction, router mounting, framework-specific routes, client-call detection, handler resolution, and linking of clients to server endpoints.
Wraps the Node-based viewer geometry and drawer-state checks as pytest tests, failing with captured JavaScript output when layout or UI state invariants break.

Command-line entry for cbi. `build_parser()` registers init, team, scan, check, worktrees, prime, status, search, show, context, tests-for, hotspots, orphans, cycles, deps, tasks, task, submit, ingest, build, diff, render, open, open-file and review, and `main()` dispatches them. `scan` writes model.db and `scan_ref` writes refs/<sha>/model.db from git objects with no checkout, both skipping a matching fingerprint; the other commands call query, graph, tasks, build, diff, render, review, open_link, editor, ingest, check and team, and `cbi task --check` validates a draft without storing it.

Tests opening already-built viewers without rescanning and the lightweight parsing used to detect project status and changed files. It also verifies safe commit lookup and stable map fingerprints when list ordering changes.

Tests the concept viewer payload built from a fixture model. Relationship rollups follow leaves and ancestors, leaves carry symbols, env, screens, tests, coverage, and externals, and a stated relationship keeps type-only imports and injection as evidence instead of calls. Stored entry and hosts attributes are read through, a reexport becomes a ghost of the defining symbol, concepts replace the deployable fallback (otherwise the view is deployables, packages, and externals), and build writes concepts.js and tree.js while escaping a closing script tag.

Tests coverage and test-result format detection and ingestion for LCOV, coverage.py JSON, and JUnit XML. It verifies line and symbol rollups, test edges, suite merging, artifact replacement, path mapping diagnostics, CLI counts, help text, and runner detection from manifests.

Pytest for the prime guide. It checks that --out names the model directory and stays out of the default guide, that prime prints the ingest commands for the detected test runners, and that task and orphans exit quietly when stdout is a closed pipe.

ViewStore saves per-project view state in the app's userData, keyed by worktree, branch or comparison: the viewer hash, which drawer sections are open, and whether the drawer is hidden. sectionTitle strips a trailing count so a section still matches after a rescan. CAPTURE_VIEW_JS reads #drawer details and the no-drawer body class, restoreScript reapplies that after the viewer renders, and writes retry through a pid-specific temp file.

Judgement tasks: generation, briefs, answer validation and the shared answer cache. summarise-files answers are cached per file content hash and other answers per input hash, across every mapped repo, so the same input is answered once; summary tasks run bottom-up from files to groups, workspaces and deployables. confirm-structure is one per workspace and writes structure.json, summarise-deployable waits for it, and submit checks the JSON against the task schema and stores the answer.

WorktreeWatch debounces directory events for 800ms and calls onFire once per burst, ignoring names under .git or .cbi and queuing one extra scan if something changes while a scan is running. Nameless events during a scan and for one second afterwards are treated as the app's own .cbi writes, and rearm reopens the watch after a short delay so macOS does not drop later events. BranchPoll checks the open branch's head every 30 seconds and calls onMove only when the commit changes, waiting until that rescan settles.

The concept map page. cbiLoad reads data/concepts.js, data/tree.js, data/diff.js, data/context.js and data/editor.js, and elk lays the boxes out. It draws relationships, comparison marks and the detail drawer, copies a node's agent block, and labels the file action Open in editor or Copy git show command.

Builds a fixture concept model and drives the static viewer with Playwright. It locks in that relationships ending on a container are drawn in incoming and outgoing lanes beside the frame, with counts matching the drawer, and that the legend lists only roles present on the diagram. Hovering or focusing a usage row shows the relationship label and resolved calls and highlights the linked edges.

Turns a folder or a file path into the git repository's main worktree and current branch name. resolveProject runs only a fixed set of read-only git commands through realGit, which uses the git executable from PATH with a 15 second timeout and no shell, and it reports a missing folder, a missing git binary, a path that is not a repository, a bare repository, or a checkout with no working tree. The main path is the parent of .git when git-common-dir ends in .git, otherwise core.worktree or show-toplevel, then realpath, and an abbrev-ref of HEAD or an empty name is returned as detached.

Loads lcov, coverage.py JSON and JUnit XML into coverage lines, test results and coverage tests edges, detecting the format from the file content. Reloading an artifact replaces only that path's earlier rows, a line counts as covered if any loaded artifact hit it, and unmatched paths or test names become unmapped_coverage diagnostics. It also turns package.json and pyproject.toml runners (node:test, vitest, jest, pytest) into the shell lines cbi prime prints.

Plans and launches safe editor commands for files shown in the viewer. It parses templates without a shell, discovers editor executables, confines paths to repositories, resolves worktrees, materializes read-only ref snapshots, and persists editor settings.

Tests persistence and restoration of viewer navigation state, including drawer sections, hashes, system tabs, comparisons, and per-worktree isolation. It also verifies graceful recovery from corrupt saved state.

Tests headless concept-map image capture. Chrome comes from the macOS app, else Program Files chrome.exe, else PATH, and skips non-executables; with none, render_images writes nothing and reports skipped; base and head write four files and delete them if head fails. Chrome is headless, own profile, no virtual time budget; not cbi-render-ready, a crash, an unknown concept, or a missing model writes nothing and exits 1; a bad compare exits 2; no Chrome exits 3; staging includes the diff; a hung browser is killed; a live capture shows App, UI, and Added, and parallel runs show App and UI.

Parser for TypeScript, TSX and JavaScript. Symbols are top-level definitions, with export unwrapped, and class members, including methods of an exported object literal. Facts for resolve.py are imports, exports, calls, literal file reads and path builds, process.env and import.meta.env reads, Cypress visits, frontend route records and HTTP routes and client calls from the shared endpoints pass; JSX and createElement calls are marked as renders, and nothing is resolved here.

Locates existing worktree or ref viewers for instant display and reads CBI status directly from immutable SQLite databases. It parses viewer payloads and computes canonical fingerprints so semantically unchanged rebuilds are not treated as updates.

Tests the SQLite model store. open_db sets a busy timeout and WAL mode, including the attached answer cache, and a read-only open of that file creates no -wal or -shm. The schema includes nodes, edges, diagnostics, file_state, coverage_lines, results, tasks, search, and meta, and opening a database whose user_version does not match rebuilds it and drops stored meta such as the fingerprint.

Produces the context-sensitive cbi prime guide for the repository containing the current directory. It reports open and blocked judgement work, explains the task loop or completed-map queries, and adds viewer, history, and detected test-ingestion guidance.

Exercises cbi:// deep-link parsing and resolution, including worktrees, refs, pull requests, comparisons, viewer navigation, and hostile inputs. It verifies all Git and GitHub CLI operations remain read-only and do not dirty repositories.

A golden dump locks TypeScript and TSX symbols, including classes, interfaces, methods, arrows, overloads, and duplicate signatures. Rescan after a rewrite keeps only the new symbol, and deleting the file removes the symbols. vitest describe.each, it.each, and test.each, and jest test.each, become suites and cases that keep the template title, a .spec.ts file is a test file, and a parse error is a diagnostic while symbols parsed before the error and in other files remain.

Tests safe repository resolution from files, nested folders, linked worktrees, submodules, detached heads, and repositories with separate Git directories. It also covers missing or bare repositories and compatibility with older Git while confirming all operations are read-only.

Tests headless viewer rendering and comparison image capture through Chrome, including executable discovery, isolated browser arguments, readiness polling, SVG preservation, and process cleanup. It verifies atomic output behavior for failures, unknown concepts, missing browsers, screen sketches, parallel renders, and CLI validation.

Imports .github/changelog_notes.py by path and tests section(). On a sample changelog, version 0.1.0 returns only that heading and 'First public release.', with no Unreleased or 0.0.1 text, and a missing 9.9.9 raises SystemExit matching 'no section for 9.9.9'. Reading the repo CHANGELOG.md for 0.1.0 must include the words cbi scan, unsigned, and Python.

Discovers repositories, submodules, worktrees, branches, commits, and tracked files, then classifies and hashes their contents. It also implements ignore rules, model fingerprints, Git object access, and inventory construction.

Lets the graph viewer open one source file in an editor, and editorButton returns the Open in editor or Copy git show command control. openInEditor calls window.cbiOpenInEditor when the desktop app injected it and toasts a notice or failure. Otherwise it copies a git show <sha>:<file> command on a static ref view, or clicks a vscode://file or cursor://file URL that editorHref builds from the cbiSetEditor root or a file: page under /.cbi/, defaulting the line to 1, leaving Windows drive letters unencoded, and toasting when the editor is none.

Tests sameViewer and sameViewerFile: the same viewer file URL and hash is already showing, a different hash or a non-viewer page (about:blank or an empty URL) needs a load, and file identity ignores the hash. A hash is not treated as part of the path when the viewer file path contains a space.

Implements team mode, where the accepted judgement is committed in .cbi/answers.jsonl and the model is rebuilt from it. It reads team.toml settings, imports and exports the sorted, merge-friendly answers file, writes git attributes and the derived .gitignore, and runs `cbi team init`. It also finds the git rule that ignores the committed judgement files and removes a plain root `.cbi` line from .gitignore automatically, reporting any other rule.

Opens one file, symbol or test for `cbi open-file` and the desktop app. A template is split into arguments and `{project}`, `{file}` and `{line}` are filled in with no shell (default `code --reuse-window {project} --goto {file}:{line}`, or cursor); the program is found on PATH, in the macOS app bundle, or with Windows `where`. `open_node()` looks the node up through `query`, refuses a concept, folder, deployable, package or external, prints the command and launches it detached; `--ref` uses a worktree that has that branch or commit, otherwise a mode 0444 copy from `git show` outside the repo.

Team mode, which commits the judgement and rebuilds the derived model. .cbi/team.toml opts in and supplies check (read by cbi check) and brief_budget (read by the part splitter); answers.jsonl is the shared answer cache, one JSON object per line, sorted so two branches can merge with union. cbi team init writes the opt-in files and prints the git commands without committing or pushing, and model.db, the viewer and ref models stay ignored.
Tests CBI executable discovery and persisted settings across environment overrides, PATH, platform-specific fallbacks, missing binaries, and damaged settings files.

Pytest for ingesting coverage and test results into the model. It detects lcov, JUnit and coverage.py by content, rolls lcov lines up to symbols, matches JUnit cases including templated names, and turns coverage.py contexts into tests edges, reporting paths and cases that do not map. Reingest replaces only that ingest's rows while suites merge, the CLI prints counts and rejects unknown files, and runner detection reads project manifests.

Detects deployables and packages from manifests after resolution, because membership follows import edges. Rules cover package.json, Vite, pyproject, wrangler.toml workers, skill and repertoire directories, Dockerfiles, compose files and .NET projects, and .cbi/structure.json then adds, renames or removes them. This step owns the deployable and package nodes, the edges whose source is manifest, and unresolved_entry diagnostics, and replaces them on every scan.

Discovers UI components, routes, templates, render relationships, and finite UI states, then manages the sketch-screens judgement task. It validates and applies submitted screen hierarchies as model nodes and sketch edges and provides detailed source-backed briefs and screen appearance queries.

Indexes markdown docs after the search rebuild on every scan the no-change shortcut does not stop. index() rereads each doc file, sets its title from YAML front matter or the first heading outside a fence, writes the title and a truncated body into the search index, and replaces mentions edges to backtick paths and uniquely named symbols.

Tests revealFor and revealWindow with a fake window that records calls. A non-headless deep link or CLI only calls showInactive, even if the window is minimized, while a dock, app, or menu activation calls show and focus, and restore first when minimized. Headless mode never calls the window, and a null or destroyed window is left alone for hidden, inactive, and focus.

Tests that section titles drop a trailing count, parseCaptured keeps the hash, drawer visibility and open sections while ignoring junk, and restoreScript plus CAPTURE_VIEW_JS refer to #drawer and no-drawer. ViewStore stores a separate hash and drawer per worktree, branch and comparison; updateHash does not clear sections, a missing key is an empty view, and a corrupt file reads as empty until the next save replaces it.

Prints the state-aware `cbi prime` guide for the current repo: an introduction when the repo is not initialised or scanned, the task loop with counts by kind and ingest commands when judgement tasks are pending, and a usage guide when the map is complete. It can read a model from --out or from a stored ref model chosen with --ref, and repeats that flag in every command it prints.

A Node script that loads the viewer page in a vm sandbox and checks its layout helpers. It asserts edge labels, merged pair edges, label placement, and that routes stay in their lanes without crossing. It prints layout checks passed when every assertion holds.

Pytest for cbi review. It checks Mermaid of changed concepts and their direct neighbours, writing the review folder and image files for a commit range without calling gh, pull-request resolution that reads gh and does not post, a narrative cached by the commit pair, and posting that creates a comment then updates it. It also covers provisional owners and the define-concepts task, a package diagram when concepts are missing, injection calls counted only outside tests, and a review that leaves the worktree and refs unchanged.

Finds a viewer already on disk and reads model status without running cbi. instantOpen returns `.cbi/viewer/index.html` for a worktree or `.cbi/refs/<sha>/viewer/index.html` for a saved branch, and a non-main folder never uses the main map. sqlite3 uses an immutable file URI; status and file_state rows are parsed; countChangedFiles counts added, removed, and rehashed paths; payloadFingerprint hashes cbiLoad JSON so reordered lists match, and isCompareScript is true when that payload is an object.

Builds a short Markdown description of one node for pasting into an agent. cbi context prints it, and cbi build embeds the same text per selectable box and symbol so the static viewer can copy it without the CLI. The block names the node, its concept chain, relationships, tests, env var names and the cbi commands to run next, and never includes env values, defaults or examples.

ProjectSession watches a model directory (default <root>/.cbi, or <root>/.cbi/refs/<sha> for a branch view) and, 400ms after model.db, its journal or its wal changes, rebuilds the viewer. It reloads the hash captured before the rebuild, then reports status and a build, ready or error progress phase. A change during a rebuild is queued as one more refresh, and stop cancels a pending one and closes the watch.

Playwright Electron smoke for the desktop update banner. On macOS it exits unless CI is set, then sets CBI_HEADLESS=1 and points CBI_UPDATE_URL at a local release server. It opens a fixture repo, checks that automatic updates default on, that a newer release shows a banner which skip hides and the menu can show again, and that a relaunch sends an etag and a codebase-inspector user agent with no Authorization header, without showing the skipped version.

Extracts HTTP route and client-call facts from a Python, TypeScript or C# syntax tree. It collects routers, mounts and route handlers (decorators and MapGet-style calls) and client calls through fetch, axios, ky, httpx, requests and thin wrappers, and treats an anchor whose href is /api or /api/... as a GET. Facts name definitions by index, a non-symbol caller is left for the file, and test files return empty lists so mock fetches are not calls.

Normalises HTTP paths and matches client calls to server routes. A route path joins every prefix that mounts its router; a client may omit a server prefix, and the match is the longest suffix that ends on a segment boundary, with {id}, :id and {id:int} treated as the same parameter kind. link reads the model's HTTP facts and returns http_calls edge rows, diagnostics and the route list stored on each handler, and it does not import resolve.

Tests confirm-structure and summarise-deployable. The brief lists detected deployables, unresolved entries, directories, and libraries; a test-only import does not make a directory a library, and empty arrays accept detection without inventing a package. A bad answer reports every check, accept writes structure.json and keeps ids, summarise-deployable stays blocked until members are summarised, a changed member summary or a hand edit reopens the task, a second repo reuses the answers, and a detection change makes them stale.

Builds an editor argv and launches it with no shell. Presets are vscode (`code --reuse-window {project} --goto {file}:{line}`), cursor, none, and a custom template that must contain {file}; tokens are split before {project}, {file}, and {line} are filled, and the program comes from PATH or the macOS app bundle. A worktree path must stay inside the checkout after realpath, a ref reuses a worktree with that branch or commit or else `git show` writes a read-only snapshot, launchEditor spawns detached, CBI_EDITOR_DRY_RUN only records argv, and a Windows .cmd runs via cmd.exe /d /s /c.

Locks private env files and which reads become nodes. Files named .env, .env.local, .env.production and .env.example.local are never opened, so secrets stay out of the database, while example and sample files are read. Scan records process.env, import.meta.env and os getenv reads with aliases, defaults and weight 2, plus example, compose and wrangler declarations; writes, deletes, dynamic keys, shadowed names and lowercase keys are dropped, a spread is an env_passthrough diagnostic, show and search list readers, and rescan drops a removed read and an unused declaration.

Read-only commands over an open model: search, show, tests-for and status, each printing text or JSON and returning an exit code. Search matches names, paths, signatures, docs and summaries, and a query containing / also matches HTTP routes. show prints one node's summary, children, relationships, linked tests and diagnostics, including injection calls, relates labels, env readers and the HTTP endpoints between concepts, and nothing here writes the model.

Playwright Electron smoke of opening a folder, switching versions, and deep links. On macOS it exits unless CI is set, then sets CBI_HEADLESS=1 and fails if a window is visible or focused. With fixture-cli on main, side-cli on side, and lane-cli in a worktree, it checks the diagram appears before a slowed scan ends, a click hash is saved and restored with the drawer, an unchanged scan does not reload, a deep link lands on a deployable, a compare link opens Changes and returns to main without changing git, and a source edit shows Map updated until Show reloads and keeps the hash.

Implements the browser viewer for concept maps, code relationships, history and comparisons, database and endpoint system views, and screen sketches. It handles navigation, layout, interaction, search, drawers, overlays, pan and zoom, and rendering of model evidence.

Builds the notes shown when a background scan finishes, without changing the map on screen. updateToast is null when the new fingerprint matches the one already shown or either fingerprint is empty; otherwise it is a Map updated note with a Show action and a file-change count. errorToast keeps the command output as detail and uses a shortened first line as the message.

Tests editor template parsing, executable discovery, safe path resolution, viewer configuration, and detached launches across platforms. It covers worktree selection for refs, immutable snapshot creation and reuse, traversal and symlink escapes, and the open-file CLI without modifying repositories.
Constructs deterministic, layout-free payloads for the database and endpoint system views from model nodes and edges, including schema details, routes, calls, summaries, and table usage.

The concept-map page. It receives concepts, diff, tree, editor and context data through cbiLoad, lays the diagram out with elk, and draws comparison marks, screen sketches, the drawer and the legend. Hash routing, search and copy-for-agent run in the page, and a double-click asks the host to open a file.
Defines the cbi command-line interface and coordinates repository scanning, model queries, judgement tasks, submission, viewer builds, history, comparisons, worktrees, and coverage ingestion.
Runs the viewer drawer logic in a minimal virtual DOM and checks that section open state persists while redrawing the same view but resets when navigation changes to another concept.

Pytest for how markdown is indexed. Titles come from front matter, otherwise the first heading outside a fence, and inline code spans and links become mentions edges while fenced code is ignored. Scan stores doc nodes and a doc collection, search finds a title and a body word, rescan replaces the title and mentions, and the default ignore drops minified CSS made of very long lines.

Implements `cbi check`, which scans the repository and reports changed code or test files that lack summaries or concept ownership, invalid or stale judgement data, and answers that resemble secrets. It resolves the comparison base, preserves committed judgement files around the scan, supports plain and GitHub annotation output, and respects team warning mode.

node:test suite for the desktop update check. It covers a newer release becoming a banner that prefers this machine's asset, same and older versions, drafts and prereleases, skip and the once-a-day automatic banner, silent failure unless the check was asked for, a 304 keeping the cached release, the auto setting defaulting on, a damaged state file, and fetch redirects, etags, and timeouts.

Tests remote-ref parsing and the git allowlist. parseRemoteRefs drops symbolic origin/HEAD, skips incomplete lines, and returns branch names sorted. The only accepted commands are git fetch --prune and git for-each-ref of refs/remotes; checkout, switch, stash, reset, clean, worktree, commit, merge, and rebase throw.

Pytest for define-concepts and the concept model. It checks that the brief lists checks, files and pairs, that a bad answer reports every failed check, kind aliases and hand-edited mechanisms, coverage that skips edges from test files, and warnings that are accepted and shown again. It also covers accept and show, rescan of a new, changed or removed file, invalid concepts JSON clearing the map, optional tracked files, symbol show grouping calls by owning concept, and validation of entry files and hosts.

Pytest for dependency-injection call edges in TypeScript and Python. It checks type-only and TYPE_CHECKING imports, structural fields, protocols, known types, remote interfaces and constructors, and reports unresolved or unannotated injection. Production scans skip test doubles, and define-concepts counts an injection edge only when its confidence is 0.6.

runProcess runs an executable with a fixed argv list, shell: false, and PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1. It streams complete stdout and stderr lines to onLine and resolves { code, stdout, stderr }. At timeoutMs it kills the child, appends a timeout line and finishes with code 1; an optional KillSlot exposes that kill function to the caller.

Headless capture for the concept map. It sets window.cbiRender, turns a cbiLoad view payload into the focus and side hash, and when app.js finishes the diagram copies the fitted SVG into #svg-out with the viewer CSS embedded and a compact key of the visible change marks. The document title becomes cbi-render-ready, or cbi-render-failed when the diagram is empty or drawing the key throws.

Projects .cbi/concepts.json into the model as a hierarchy beside the file tree and owns the define-concepts judgement task. Leaves own files through owns edges; relates edges store label, via, at and kind, and entry is derived from deployable entry points unless a hosts relationship or an explicit flag overrides it. apply replaces concept nodes on every scan; problems, refresh and accept validate and close answers so every code and test file belongs to exactly one leaf and cross-concept production calls are covered by a relationship.

The only git commands the version switcher adds. FETCH_ARGV is fetch --prune and REMOTES_ARGV is for-each-ref of refs/remotes; assertRemoteArgv throws on anything else. parseRemoteRefs reads the nul-separated short name and object id, drops symbolic origin/HEAD, and returns RemoteRef entries sorted by name.

Tests `cbi check` on team repos: secret detection that skips hex and prose, errors outside a repo or before init, changed code that needs a summary, branch files that pass once their tasks are answered, stale answers, secrets, warn mode annotations, invalid JSON files, and a report of the ignore rule that hides the judgement files. It also checks that the team brief budget overrides the environment and that the README carries the team init snippet.

Tests comparison planning. gh is limited to pr view with --json baseRefOid,headRefOid, and the JSON must contain both commit shas. planCompare takes two sides (worktree, branch, or commit) or a pull request number instead, and refuses a missing side, a bad PR, an unknown worktree, a flag-like branch name, and injected or range refs.

Parses and validates cbi://open URLs, resolves repository worktrees or immutable refs, and prepares viewer targets for normal and comparison links. It constrains node IDs, paths, refs, Git commands, and GitHub CLI calls to prevent traversal and command injection.

Defines the complete cbi command-line interface and dispatch for initialization, scanning worktrees or refs, querying, judgement tasks, review, history, diffs, builds, editor opening, worktree inventory, and test ingestion. It coordinates model locations and scan fingerprints, opens read-only models for queries, validates task submissions, and handles platform output and broken pipes.

Tests that paths under .git or .cbi, plus null and empty names, do not schedule a rescan. WorktreeWatch collapses a burst into one scan, queues exactly one more scan for a change during a scan, does not chain a nameless event during a scan, reopens the watch on rearm without dropping a running scan, and stop cancels a pending scan. BranchPoll calls onMove only when the head changes, ignores a tick after stop, and uses a 30s interval (RESCAN_DEBOUNCE_MS is at least 400).

Locks the compare viewer payload in data/diff.js. A compare build writes a diff object with base and head labels, concept-added, concept-removed, symbol-changed and integration-added, the removed concept and its relationship, source for changed functions but not components, provisional ids and the base screen text, escaping < as a unicode escape; without compare the payload is null. The flag rejects a three-dot range and rejects --compare combined with --ref.

Pytest for JavaScript and TypeScript manifests. package.json, Vite and tsconfig turn entry points into deployables mapped to source, part_of follows imports and package names, and a bin that maps to no file is an unresolved-entry diagnostic. Verify and tooling scripts are not deployables, and a second fixture covers a shared package, a dist bin, an OpenNext worker, and structure.json adding, renaming and removing packages.

Validates the desktop application installer shell script contract, including expected platform checks, commands, paths, safety properties, and exit behavior. It accounts for locating a usable Bash implementation on Windows.

Prints the guide for the repo that contains the current directory. An unmapped repo gets the init and scan steps, a repo with open tasks gets the task counts and the submit loop, and a finished map gets example query commands. When the model is stored outside the repo, every command in the guide includes the --out flag.

Paths for the Electron icons. windowIcon is the PNG packed at build/icon.png; the icns is the bundle icon. dockIcon returns that PNG only in dev, and a packaged app returns null so macOS keeps the icon registered for the installed bundle.

Tests RecentsStore, the saved list of recent projects. Opening stores a project named from its path, unpinned with an empty last view, and moves it to the front; opening again updates lastOpened but keeps the name, pin and last view, and pinned entries stay above newer unpinned ones. Rename only trims the display name and refuses an empty one, remove drops an entry, relocate retargets a missing path keeping name and pin or drops it when the new path is already listed, last view is stored without reordering, a damaged file reads as empty, and the file on disk is the saved list.

Tests scanning a branch, tag or commit from git objects into a stored ref model: both branches map without a checkout, `cbi prime --ref` prints a guide whose commands carry the resolved --ref, the worktree and refs stay untouched (checked with a git shim), ref tasks reuse the answer cache, and `cbi worktrees --json` lists worktrees and branches.
