Decides how the desktop window may appear. revealFor returns hidden when headless, inactive for a CLI or deep link, and focus for a dock click, the app icon, or a menu. revealWindow ignores a hidden request and a missing or destroyed window, calls only showInactive in inactive mode and does not call restore, show, or focus, and in focus mode restores a minimized window and then calls show and focus.

Loads viewer layout helpers in a Node VM and exercises geometry, edge routing, label placement, grouping, screen pairing, and related rendering invariants. It uses synthetic diagrams to detect overlaps, invalid paths, and unstable layout behavior without a browser.

Stores recent projects in the app's userData file, never in the repository. RecentsStore records an open, pin, rename, remove, relocate, the last viewer hash, and the cached Projects-row snapshot, writing through a temporary file. Reading drops malformed entries and sorts pinned items first, then most recently opened.

A Node script that loads viewer app.js in a fake DOM and checks screen-region markup. A region whose when is non-blank gets the cond and wf classes and a cond-tag showing the trimmed condition; a blank when stays plain with no tag.

Tests cbi --version, cbi --help, cbi prime on a repo with no model, and the make_repo helper. --version exits 0 with 'cbi 0.1.0', the same version as pyproject.toml and app/package.json, and --help exits 0 and contains every command name in COMMANDS. prime prints cbi init, cbi scan, --out DIR, and 'must stay untouched' in fewer than 60 lines and does not create .cbi, and make_repo commits the supplied files and leaves git status --porcelain empty.

Detects test runners from project manifests, prints suitable coverage commands, and ingests LCOV, coverage.py JSON, and JUnit XML artifacts into the model. It maps artifact paths and test identities to nodes, replaces prior rows per artifact, merges coverage evidence, and reports unmapped diagnostics.

Tests architecture history: point selection that keeps direct commits before the first merge and then only merges, falling back to plain commits when there are no merges, projection of current concepts onto moved files with folder guesses, the `cbi history` command writing Markdown and reusing point models, and narratives from summarise-change appearing in the outputs.
Extracts relational schemas and table usage from SQL and supported ORM frameworks. It merges declarations and writes derived table, column, constraint, and code-usage nodes and edges into the model.

Safely opens mapped source nodes in a configured editor using argument templates without invoking a shell. It validates repository-relative paths, discovers executables cross-platform, resolves files in matching worktrees or creates read-only commit snapshots, and launches detached editor processes.
Tests deterministic database and endpoint payload generation and verifies that builds emit the corresponding system-view data scripts.

Parser for a Vue single-file component. Each script block is parsed as TypeScript or JavaScript and its line numbers are shifted onto the .vue file, and the component symbol is the file's default export, named after the file. Template tags that name an imported component become calls with the same jsx marker JSX uses, and an anchor in the template whose href is /api/... is a GET call on the component.

Implements cbi check. It scans so the derived model is current, then restores judgement files so answers.jsonl and the JSON maps stay as they were, and it does not fetch, commit or push. It fails when a changed code or test file has no summary or, once concepts exist, no owning concept, when structure.json, concepts.json or screens.json fail their checks, when team-mode answers.jsonl is missing or stale, or when an answer contains a key or token.
Uses browser-driven system tests to verify database-view interaction, navigation state, history and comparison behavior, capture routing, and readable layout for large schemas.

Playwright Electron smoke of opening a folder, switching versions, and deep links. On macOS it exits unless CI is set, then sets CBI_HEADLESS=1 and CBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 and fails if a window is visible or focused. With fixture-cli on main, side-cli on side, and lane-cli in a worktree, it checks the diagram appears before a slowed scan ends, a click hash is saved and restored with the drawer, an unchanged scan does not reload, a deep link lands on a deployable, a compare link opens Changes and returns to main without changing git, and a source edit shows Map updated until Show reloads.

Tests parseInventory (keeps complete worktree and branch rows, drops blank ones) and buildEntries (lane labels, model state, remotes hidden until fetched, origin/HEAD omitted, unsafe refs refused). A checked-out branch opens its worktree and a branch with none is a read-only ref; a nested folder prefers that worktree, opening main restores the last key, a missing saved worktree falls through to main, and a comparison is not restored as the last version. Also checks formatScanned and refInstruction.

ViewStore saves per-project view state in the app's userData, keyed by worktree, branch or comparison: the viewer hash, which drawer sections are open, and whether the drawer is hidden. sectionTitle strips a trailing count so a section still matches after a rescan. CAPTURE_VIEW_JS reads #drawer details and the no-drawer body class, restoreScript reapplies that after the viewer renders, and updateHash changes only the hash while lastKey remembers the last selection.

Electron main for Codebase Inspector: a BrowserWindow, a sandboxed WebContentsView, the cbi:// protocol, and a single instance (macOS open-url, Windows and Linux argv). IPC handles folder open, recents, cbi and editor settings, open-in-editor, version switch, `git fetch --prune`, compare, and toasts; instantOpen shows a built viewer before a scan, otherwise cbi scans and builds, and a later build waits on the toast. Worktree watches and branch polling rescan, `cbi build --compare` (two refs or `gh pr view`) does not watch the worktree, and CBI_HEADLESS=1 hides the window and yields focus.

Playwright smoke of comparison mode, opened from file://. It builds a two-commit fixture with this worktree's cbi, seeds base and head concept maps, and checks added, removed, changed, and provisional marks, a new integration line, the legend, a plain-text code diff, the base and head toggle, before and after wireframes, and the narrow changes panel. Screenshots go to /tmp/cbi-p29-smoke.

One test on a generated repo of about 1,500 files in six packages. Four summarise-files tasks submit successfully in parallel while the database is locked, confirm-structure accepts an empty map, and the define-concepts brief splits into parts that each fit the budget, including one part per package and a cross-area part. Checking a complete answer prints ok and does not write concepts.json.

Prints one Keep a Changelog section to stdout. Given a version such as v0.1.0 and a path to CHANGELOG.md, section() drops a leading v, finds the line starting with ## [version], and returns that block up to but not including the next ## heading, followed by a newline. It exits with an error when it is not given a version and a changelog path, or when that heading is missing.

Pytest coverage for scanning a branch, tag, or commit from git objects without a checkout, and for the worktrees JSON listing. A two-branch fixture with a real submodule and a missing gitlink checks per-commit models under .cbi/refs, shared versus branch-only files, ignored secrets, model reuse, and that the scan only calls read-only git. It also checks judgement answers are reused across a rescan and the other branch, and that worktrees --json reports lanes, detached heads, model completeness, and which branches already have a ref model.

Splits oversized judgement briefs into byte-budgeted parts while preserving coherent package, deployable, concept, and screen sections. It also formats part indexes and prime guidance for large repositories or numerous file-summary batches.
Provides basic CLI contract tests for package version output, command help coverage, Windows UTF-8 output configuration, initial prime guidance, and the temporary repository fixture.
Empty package marker so src/cbi imports as the cbi package. It defines no names and re-exports nothing.
Renders viewer pages and image captures from built CBI artifacts, coordinating browser availability, output paths, navigation targets, and capture options.

Script for the shell page. It draws the start screen (recent projects, the cbi path, and the editor choice), the project chrome (branch, task counts, scan progress, and the map-update toast), and the worktree, branch, and remote switcher plus the compare form. Actions go through window.cbi, and it reports the map stage's bounds so the main process can place the viewer.

Node script that loads the viewer scripts in a vm sandbox and checks graph drawing. It asserts edge-label text and class merging, label separation away from boxes, ELK label placement, external grouping, frame routing, and how a container relationship attaches to the child the code reaches. It prints that the checks passed, or exits non-zero when an assertion fails.

Splits a define-concepts or sketch-screens brief that exceeds the size budget, while the answer stays one JSON document. Concepts become one part per package or deployable (that area's files, summaries, symbol outlines and internal pairs) plus a cross-area part; screens become one part per UI deployable, the page tree from its entries, with each component's JSX left whole. The budget is team.toml brief_budget, else CBI_BRIEF_BUDGET, else 150 KB.

Implements the lifecycle for CBI judgement tasks, shared answer caching, dependency-aware summary refresh, task briefs, schemas, validation, and atomic submission. It manages file, group, deployable, workspace, structure, and change tasks, applies accepted answers to the model and JSON documents, and reports newly unblocked work.

Tests ignore rules, file classification, C# test roots, and doc collections. Ignore follows gitignore syntax, including anchored paths, negations, and directory-only rules. classify maps paths to code, test, doc, or other, including Cypress e2e specs, Vue tests, and C# files under a *.Tests or *.Testing project directory, and a doc collection is a directory of more than 100 files that is mostly markdown with little code.

Pytest coverage of Vue single-file components, treating script blocks as TypeScript and template tags as renders. Direct parser tests check that /api hrefs become GET calls on the component (none in a spec), that a default-exported function becomes a documented component whose template calls resolve to imported components, and that script setup names the component from the filename while keeping real source lines for functions and routes. A scanned fixture then checks component, function, and test nodes, jsx call edges, tests edges from the colocated spec, and a golden dump of the model.

Pytest for repository identity helpers. SSH, HTTPS and git-protocol forms of one GitHub repository normalise to the same id, while local and file URLs use the directory name with a local: prefix. repo_name keeps the remote path's case and returns None for a blank URL, and a relative submodule URL resolves against the parent remote.

Ranks and checks the import graph: hotspots() orders files, folders, packages and concepts by fan-in, fan-out, lines or symbol count, and orphans() lists production code nothing else in production references, test-only exports, and files no deployable entry reaches. collect_cycles() and record_cycles() find import cycles among production files, their folders and their packages and store cycle diagnostics. deps() prints a dependency matrix and exits 1 when a --forbid layering rule is broken.

Tests team mode end to end: `cbi team init` exporting answers without committing, removing only a plain root .cbi ignore rule and reporting other rules, keeping an existing .gitattributes in the map, ignoring answers when team mode is off, and --out leaving the repo untouched. It also covers skipping bad rows on import, importing a changed answers file, a clone with no open tasks and the same concept map, and two branches merging answers without a conflict. Its helpers are reused by test_check.py.

Tests selection of default-branch history points, projection of present concepts onto moved historical files, model reuse, and Markdown changelog generation. It also verifies summarise-change narratives are cached and included in history outputs.

Locates the cbi CLI and persists its path in settings JSON. findCbi tries CBI_BIN, then the saved path, then PATH, then ~/.local/bin/cbi (cbi.exe on Windows, with a where fallback). A set path that is not executable is an error that includes the `uv tool install .` hint, and a missing or damaged settings file reads as cbiPath null.

Node id rules and git remote normalisation. normalise_remote() turns ssh and https URLs of one repo into a single lowercased host/owner/repo (a local path becomes local:<dirname>); resolve_relative_url() resolves a .gitmodules relative URL against the parent remote. file_id(), group_id() and symbol_ids() build file, directory and symbol ids, suffixing repeated qualified names with a signature hash.

SQLite model store for a scanned repo: schema version 6 (nodes, edges, diagnostics, parse facts, file state, coverage, test results, tasks, FTS search, and meta) is created on open, or the file is deleted and rebuilt when the version differs. Writable connections use WAL with a 30s busy timeout and retry locked writes; read-only opens do not create the database or journal files. Scan replaces file state and workspace, group, file, and doc nodes, swaps one file's symbols, tests, facts, and LOC, drops orphans, sets diagnostics, and rebuilds search rows so HTTP route method and path are indexed.

Validates comparison form input and produces safe plans for comparing worktrees, branches, commits, or GitHub pull requests. It strictly validates refs, commit hashes, and the single allowed read-only gh command.

Defines and validates the worktree, branch, remote, and comparison targets shown by the application's version switcher. It parses CBI inventory data, restores selections, chooses an initial target from picked folders and saved state, and builds labeled entries with mapping status while rejecting unsafe refs.

Tests that read commands open a model they cannot write and do not create a journal. A read-only connection on a mode-444 database, with a mode-444 answer cache, still reads nodes and the cache and creates no -wal or -shm, and does not create a cache directory when the cache path is missing. status, search, show, tests-for, hotspots, orphans, cycles, deps, and context, including status --ref, succeed on a chmod copy of a scanned model and leave no sidecars.

Tests editor templates and open-file. Quotes and ';' stay one argument, line 0 becomes 1, and a blank or unclosed template is code 2; traversal, absolute paths, NUL, '.', missing files, and outside symlinks fail; inside symlinks open. A ref opens a worktree for the branch or commit, else a reused 0444 snapshot, no checkout; files, symbols, and test cases open, not folders, symlinks, or suites; PATH beats the bundle and code.cmd beats code.exe; launch is not a shell; unknown editors become vscode; caches are AppData, XDG, or Library/Caches; greet uses --goto and a folder or editor none exits 1.

Drives src/cbi/viewer/open-editor.js inside a Node vm, with no browser, and checks vscode:// file hrefs. A Unix root keeps the leading slash (vscode://file/Users/me/repo/src/a.ts:1). A Windows drive stays unencoded (vscode://file/C:/repo/src/a.ts:4), a space becomes %20, and a file: pathname /C:/repo/.cbi/viewer/index.html drops the extra slash so the href is vscode://file/C:/repo/src/a.ts:1.

Electron main for Codebase Inspector: a BrowserWindow, a sandboxed WebContentsView, the cbi:// protocol, and a single instance (macOS open-url, Windows and Linux argv). IPC handles folder open, recents, cbi and editor settings, open-in-editor, version switch, git fetch, compare, toasts, and a GitHub update check that shows a banner and opens the notes or asset in the browser. Worktree watches and branch polling rescan, a compare build does not watch the worktree, CBI_HEADLESS=1 hides the window, and CBI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 skips the automatic check.

cbi review resolves a pull request, branch, commit or base..head range, scans both commits without checking out or writing the working tree, and writes .cbi/reviews/<base>..<head>/review.md. The file has a cbi://open link, change counts, a Mermaid flowchart of changed concepts (or deployables, packages and folders) and their direct neighbours, plus untested changes and integration points. It opens a summarise-change task and, for unowned head files, a provisional define-concepts task, captures before/after images, and --post creates or edits the GitHub comment that carries <!-- cbi-review -->.

Writes a PNG and an SVG of the concept map by capturing the viewer in headless system Chrome or Chromium. `render_images`, called by `cbi review`, writes before.png, before.svg, after.png and after.svg of the top level from a base and head model and a `diff.compare` change list, or skips when Chrome is missing. `render_view`, called by `cbi render`, stages render.html plus data/view.js, data/diff.js and data/model.js from `build.concept_view`, waits for the title cbi-render-ready, reads #svg-out and the screenshot over the DevTools websocket, then kills the browser.
Tests SQL and ORM schema extraction for SQLAlchemy, Django, Prisma, TypeORM, and EF Core, including declaration merging and attachment of table usage to functions.

Implements the browser-based interactive architecture viewer for concept maps, source symbols, integrations, screens, comparisons, and history. It loads generated data, manages URL-driven navigation and search, lays out and renders SVG diagrams with ELK, routes edges and labels, supports zoom and keyboard interaction, and populates details, legends, overlays, and agent-copy controls.

Preload for the shell window. With context isolation on, it exposes window.cbi for picking and opening a folder, recents, the cbi binary and editor settings, version switching, compare, toasts, and progress, and it sends a dropped file's path to the main process. Each subscription returns an unsubscribe function.

Tests HTTP routes, client calls, and the edges that join them. Path templates, TypeScript request wrappers, Python f-strings, C# attributes, and minimal APIs become method and path pairs, and a scan links clients to handlers with a confidence, reports unmatched calls, and ignores calls in test files. Exported object methods are symbols whose calls resolve to the handler, nested and unexported objects are not, and an href that starts with /api on JSX or a Vue template is a GET on that component.

Parses and validates cbi://open URLs (repo, ref, node, compare, pr) and picks a cbi:// argument out of argv for a second instance. An absolute ref opens that worktree with watching on; a branch or commit is checked with read-only git rev-parse and opens the ref viewer with watching off. compare must be base..head, and pr runs `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefOid,headRefOid` before both SHAs are verified; shell metacharacters, `..`, repeated keys, and mixing compare, pr, and ref are refused, and viewerLocation builds the hash chips c or s plus from and bh.

answer.summary: Comprehensive pytest and browser-driven test suite for repository scanning, parsing, model construction, judgement workflows, queries, viewer behavior, desktop integration, rendering, diffs, reviews, and safety constraints.

Playwright Electron smokes for the desktop app. They run headless, and on macOS they run only when CI is set. editor-ref.mjs opens a symbol on a ref that is not checked out, smoke.mjs opens a folder, switches versions, and follows deep links, and update-smoke.mjs checks the update banner against a local release server.

Electron desktop shell for Codebase Inspector. It opens a git repository, runs the installed cbi CLI to init, scan and build, and shows the viewer that build writes, including a banner when a newer release is available. src holds the main process, scripts copies the window HTML into dist, and test runs the Playwright smokes.

Implements the Electron desktop application that discovers CBI, maps repositories and immutable refs, displays generated viewers, and manages project, version, comparison, editor, update, and recent-state workflows. It includes sandboxed preload bridges, safe process and Git helpers, the shell renderer and styling, and comprehensive Node tests.

Implements the Electron desktop application, including its main and renderer processes, secure preload bridges, project and version selection, scanning and viewer orchestration, editor integration, persistence, update checks, and focused unit tests.

Python package behind the cbi command. It enumerates and parses a repository, stores the model in SQLite, detects deployables, and runs judgement tasks. The same package serves queries, diffs, reviews, the static viewer, image capture and editor launch.

Python package behind the cbi command. It enumerates and parses a repository, stores the model in SQLite, detects deployables, and runs judgement tasks. The same package serves queries, diffs, reviews, the static viewer, image capture, editor launch, and a cached check for a newer GitHub release.

Contains the cross-platform pytest and Node test suite for the CLI, scanners and parsers, judgement workflow, model store, queries, viewer, desktop integration, reviews, history, and security boundaries. Fixtures build isolated Git repositories and the tests use golden models, synthetic browser DOMs, Playwright, and executable stand-ins to cover end-to-end behavior without mutating source repositories.

Core Python package for the cbi CLI. It discovers and parses repositories, builds and queries the SQLite model, manages judgement tasks and concept maps, computes diffs and reviews, and produces the static viewer, system views, renders, and architecture history.

The static concept-map page and the headless capture that reuses it. app.js lays out and draws the diagram, open-editor.js opens one file in an editor or copies a git show command, and render.js copies the fitted SVG once the diagram is ready. The folder also holds the page HTML, the stylesheet and the vendored elk layout library.
Build helper for the Electron app. copy-assets.mjs creates app/dist and copies src/index.html and src/style.css into it.

Pytest and Node checks for the cbi CLI, the parsers, the model and the static viewer. The modules cover scan, resolution, concepts, tasks, diff, review, the editor and the update check, and tests/golden holds the locked text and JSON dumps they compare against. conftest.py builds a temporary git repo and points the answer cache and the update check away from the user's machine.

Electron desktop shell for Codebase Inspector. It opens a git repository, runs the installed cbi CLI to init, scan and build, and shows the viewer that build writes. src holds the main process, scripts copies the window HTML into dist, and test runs the Playwright smokes.

Electron source for the desktop app, with node:test files beside the modules. main.ts owns the window, the cbi:// protocol and IPC.
